summary: This Dockerfile creates a Ubuntu container with a few lightweight tools (jq, curl, certificates) installed for working with JSON data and making web requests. It sets up a demo directory with a pre-baked sample JSON file so examples can run without needing network access, customizes the shell prompt to show a whale emoji, and starts an interactive bash shell when the container runs.

explanations.3: This tells the installer to skip interactive prompts during setup—useful in Docker since there's no human at the keyboard to answer questions.
explanations.6: The --no-install-recommends flag tells apt to skip optional packages it would normally suggest, keeping the image smaller.
explanations.10: After installing packages, this deletes the apt cache files to reduce the final image size, since we won't need to install anything else.
explanations.16: This writes a hardcoded JSON response (formatted as a single line with printf) to a file, simulating what the randomuser.me API would return, so demos work offline.
explanations.22: This appends a custom shell prompt string to the bashrc file; the \e sequences are color codes, and the whale emoji 🐳 visually signals you're inside a container.
explanations.24: This sets bash to run in interactive mode (-i) by default when someone starts the container, so they get a live shell prompt they can type into.
